abstract: This systematic review examines the application of artificial intelligence in healthcare administration, focusing on three key areas: medical coding, patient scheduling, and operational costs. The analysis demonstrates that AI systems significantly outperform human coders in accuracy while simultaneously reducing patient no-show rates and overall administrative expenses.
keyFindings: AI medical coding achieves 95% accuracy compared to 90% for human coders, representing a 5 percentage point improvement.
AI-driven scheduling systems reduce no-show rates by 25%.
Administrative cost reduction from AI implementation is estimated at 20-35%.
methodology: Systematic review of AI applications in healthcare administration. Specific data sources, sample size, study selection criteria, and analytical approach not specified in excerpt.
